skill.name: building-agent-tools
skill.description: Guide for creating effective tools for AI agents. Use when building MCP tools, agent APIs, or any tool interface that agents will consume. Focuses on token efficiency, meaningful context, and proper namespacing.
skill.summary: Practical guidance for designing concise, useful tool interfaces for AI agents.
skill.author: Byunk

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code examples and ordinary prose in SKILL.md. No executable code, shell invocation, system reconnaissance, data exfiltration intent, or prompt injection evidence was found.

static_findings.snippet: - Example: `schedule_event` that checks availability AND creates event
- Prefix related tools with service name: `asana_projects_search`, `asana_users_search`
- Use descriptive `name` and `description` in tool schema
- Define `inputSchema` with JSON Schema for parameters
- Avoid simple CRUD-style tools that require multiple calls
- Include parameter constraints and valid values

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 35 is a Markdown inline code example for a tool name. It is prose guidance, not Ruby or shell execution.
Line 39 uses Markdown inline code to show namespaced tool names. There is no executable context or command invocation.
Line 46 references a parameter name inside Markdown backticks. It does not execute code or construct a shell command.
Line 73 references schema field names inside Markdown backticks. The file is documentation and contains no runnable Ruby or shell syntax.
Line 74 references inputSchema as an MCP schema field. This is documentation text, not command execution.
Line 36 discusses avoiding overly granular CRUD-style tools. It does not request system inspection or reconnaissance.
Line 58 recommends documenting parameter constraints and valid values. This is API design guidance, not system reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Agent tools often fail when interfaces are vague, noisy, or too granular. This skill gives practical patterns for concise names, schemas, responses, and validation.
actual_capabilities: Explains a workflow for purpose, interface design, implementation, and validation.
Recommends consolidated tools, namespacing, context-rich output, and token efficiency.
Lists anti-patterns such as granular tools, raw IDs, vague descriptions, and weak errors.
Describes MCP tool registration basics with names, descriptions, and input schemas.
Guides response formatting with structured output, success indicators, and actionable errors.
limitations: Does not generate complete MCP server implementations by itself.
Does not include runnable code templates or automated tests.
Does not cover authentication, authorization, or secret handling in depth.
Requires users to adapt guidance to their agent platform.

use_cases.title: Design a new MCP tool family
use_cases.description: Plan names, parameters, responses, and validation before implementation.

use_cases.title: Improve existing agent APIs
use_cases.description: Reduce noisy outputs, unclear parameters, and repeated calls in current tools.

use_cases.title: Review tool quality before release
use_cases.description: Check whether tools give agents enough context with minimal token cost.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Tool Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design an agent tool for this workflow: [workflow]. Ask clarifying questions, then propose purpose, name, inputs, and output.

prompt_templates.title: Consolidate Tool Operations
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these planned tools: [tool list]. Suggest which operations should be consolidated and explain the agent workflow benefit.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Tool Responses
prompt_templates.prompt: Improve this tool response format: [current response]. Make it concise, structured, and useful for the agent's next step.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an Agent Tool Interface
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this tool interface for agent usability: [interface description]. Identify naming, schema, token, pagination, and error recovery issues.

output_examples.input: A team wants separate tools for checking calendars, creating events, and inviting attendees.
output_examples.output: Recommendation: combine the common scheduling workflow into one higher-level tool with clear inputs and concise availability results.

output_examples.input: An agent API returns internal IDs and long records for every search result.
output_examples.output: Recommendation: return human-readable identifiers, relevant metadata, and pagination controls so agents can choose the next action.

output_examples.input: A tool description only says that it updates tasks.
output_examples.output: Recommendation: describe when to use the tool, required fields, valid values, returned status, and recovery steps for failures.

best_practices: Design tools around complete agent workflows, not only database operations.
Use clear names, parameter constraints, and predictable structured responses.
Validate tools with real agent tasks and measure token use.
anti_patterns: Creating many small tools that force repeated calls for common workflows.
Returning raw IDs or large records without useful context.
Writing vague descriptions or errors that do not guide recovery.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you design tool interfaces that AI agents can use reliably and efficiently.

faq.question: Does it generate a full MCP server?
faq.answer: No. It provides design guidance for tool names, schemas, responses, and validation.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance applies to agent-facing tools used by Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it before building or revising tools that agents will call during workflows.

faq.question: Does it cover security controls?
faq.answer: Only indirectly. You should still design separate authentication, authorization, and data protection controls.

faq.question: What is the main design principle?
faq.answer: Give agents meaningful context with clear interfaces and avoid unnecessary token cost.
